Indian comedy has not moved beyond slapstick, and the nation's movie channels get rights to films that just about make the B category. And talking about film, Bollywood seems to have entrenched its tentacles across Indian television. The awful tradition of melodramatic plots and multiple zoom-ins that defined 60s Hindi cinema has recently been discovered by the soaps, while the wardrobe of our television 'stars' continues to be inspired by Karan Johar's candy-flossed dreams. The only difference being that K. Jo can afford that Manhattan designer, while Ektaa Kapoor has to settle for an Andheri darzi. Indian pop also seems to have given up the fight and surrendered coveted air space on music channels to the likes of Himesh Reshammiya and Co. The only consolation that Channel (V) has to offer is the rise of its outrageously funny 'beauty on duty', Lola Kutty, the only original 'Indian' offering in my mind.
The one blessing for Indian television comes in the guise of an exhausted national cricket team. The more packed their schedule, the more the chance of us being collectively entertained or equally disheartened. Undeniable proof of the fact that television is truly a medium for all.
